value.body: A two-year master's after B.Optom focused on advanced clinical work — contact lenses, low vision, binocular vision, paediatric optometry and ocular disease management — plus a research project. It is offered by a limited number of universities and eye-care institutes.

items.label: Students enrolled
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, programme-wise enrolment, all modes (Ministry of Education)

items.label: Regulator
items.value: National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions
items.note: Set up under the NCAHP Act, 2021

value.title: How you get in
value.body: B.Optom (usually four years including an internship). Admission is through the institute's or university's own entrance test and interview, or on merit.

value.title: At a glance
items: Seats are few, so options may mean moving cities.
It leads to senior clinical roles in eye hospitals and specialty clinics, teaching (often with a Ph.D.), and roles with contact-lens and ophthalmic companies.
Clinical practice and optical retail are open after B.Optom too; the M.Optom mainly adds specialisation and teaching eligibility.
